brief.title: The Gaslamp Quay
brief.premise: A tide-clock inspector in a fog-bound port city investigates the death of a lamplighter found drowned in a locked lamp-house, and discovers that the harbour board has been selling false curfews.
constraints: Nothing supernatural: every event must have a natural explanation.

world.name: Gaslamp Quay
world.description: Gaslamp Quay is a fog-bound estuary port lit by coal gas and ruled by the Harbour Board, where curfews are bought and sold.

locations.name: Lamp-House Row
locations.description: A terrace of locked lamp-houses where gas lamps are filled and tended each dusk.

locations.name: Harbour Board Hall
locations.description: The marble hall where curfews, tide tables and mooring licences are issued.

locations.name: Fog Wharf
locations.description: A timber wharf where fog off the estuary hides ships and smugglers alike.

locations.name: Tide-Clock Tower
locations.description: A brass clock tower whose gearing tracks the tides and sets the city's curfew bell.

factions.name: Lamplighters' Guild
factions.description: A guild that fills, lights and locks the city's gas lamps.

factions.name: Harbour Board
factions.description: Officials who issue curfews and mooring licences, and profit from both.

factions.name: Fog Runners
factions.description: Smugglers who use the curfew gaps to slip cargo past the wharf.

rules.statement: The city is lit by coal gas and driven by clockwork and steam.
After the curfew bell, wharf gates are locked until dawn and may be opened only by a Harbour Board officer's key.
Each lamp-house is locked at dusk with a guild key; only the lamplighter assigned to it and the guild master hold keys.
Fog thickens on the wharf at the turn of the tide, hiding ships for about an hour.

history.name: Laying of the Gas Mains
history.description: The Harbour Board laid the first coal-gas mains along Lamp-House Row.

history.name: Raising of the Tide-Clock
history.description: Clockmakers raised the Tide-Clock Tower and tied the curfew bell to its tide gearing.

history.name: The Lamplighters' Charter
history.description: The Lamplighters' Guild won a charter granting its members exclusive keys to the lamp-houses.

history.name: The First False Curfew
history.description: The Harbour Board secretly rang an early curfew bell so that the Fog Runners could bribe an officer to unlock the wharf gates.

conflicts.name: The False Curfews
conflicts.description: The Lamplighters' Guild accuses the Harbour Board of selling false curfews.

conflicts.name: The Wharf Smuggling
conflicts.description: The Harbour Board quietly tolerates the Fog Runners' smuggling in return for bribes.

characters.name: Cato Wren
characters.description: A tide-clock inspector who checks the Tide-Clock Tower's gearing against the tide tables each month.
characters.motivation: To find out who left a lamplighter drowned in a locked lamp-house.
characters.goal: Work out who held a key to the lamp-house that night.
characters.flaw: Pursues a theory past the evidence.
characters.internal_conflict: He owes the Harbour Board his post.

abilities.name: Gear-reading
abilities.description: Spots a mistimed curfew bell by the sound of the gearing.

characters.arc: Cato learns that the curfews were sold, and that his own tables were used to justify them.

characters.name: Marguerite Ashby
characters.description: Master of the Lamplighters' Guild, who holds one of the keys to every lamp-house.
characters.motivation: To clear her Guild's name after a lamplighter's death.
characters.goal: Hand Cato the Guild's key logs.
characters.flaw: Shields her people even when they are wrong.
characters.internal_conflict: She suspects one of her own.

abilities.name: Lamp-lore
abilities.description: Knows every lamp-house's filling schedule by heart.

characters.arc: Marguerite accepts that protecting the Guild means exposing a member.

characters.name: Osric Dunne
characters.description: A Harbour Board officer who sells early curfews and holds a key that opens the wharf gates after the bell.
characters.motivation: To keep the curfew trade profitable and quiet.
characters.goal: Pin the lamplighter's death on the Guild.
characters.internal_conflict: He is unsettled that the dead man was a friend.
characters.external_conflict: Cato's inquiry threatens to expose the trade.

abilities.name: Bribe-brokering
abilities.description: Arranges payments between smugglers and the Board without a written trace.

characters.arc: Osric's network unravels as Cato matches curfew bells to payments.

relationships.description: Marguerite shares the Guild's key logs with Cato.
Cato's inquiry threatens Osric's curfew trade.
Marguerite accuses Osric of selling false curfews.

storyboard.title: The Gaslamp Quay
storyboard.logline: Cato traces a drowned lamplighter's death to a trade in false curfews.

scenes.title: The Locked Room
scenes.summary: Marguerite shows Cato the locked lamp-house where a lamplighter was found drowned with his clothes soaked in estuary water.
scenes.conflict: Only the assigned lamplighter and the guild master held keys.
scenes.outcome: Cato notes that the door was locked and that only the dead man and Marguerite held keys.

scenes.title: The Early Bell
scenes.summary: Cato checks the Tide-Clock Tower's gearing and finds the curfew bell rang an hour early on the night of the death.
scenes.goal: Check the bell against the tide tables.
scenes.conflict: The Harbour Board holds the bell records.
scenes.outcome: He learns the curfew was rung early and the wharf gates were locked early.

scenes.title: The Smuggler
scenes.summary: At Fog Wharf, Cato questions a smuggler who admits the early bell let a cargo slip past the gates with an officer's key.
scenes.goal: Learn who opened the wharf gates.
scenes.conflict: The Fog Runners fear the Board's reprisals.
scenes.outcome: The smuggler names Osric as the officer with the key.

scenes.title: The Denial
scenes.summary: Cato confronts Osric, who admits only that officers hold keys to the wharf gates.
scenes.goal: Pin the early bell on Osric.
scenes.outcome: Osric hints the Guild killed its own man to cover a theft.

scenes.title: The Key Logs
scenes.summary: Osric, the Guild master, hands Cato the Guild's key logs, which show the dead lamplighter signed his lamp-house key out at dusk and never signed it back.
scenes.conflict: The Guild fears the logs will condemn one of its own.
scenes.outcome: Cato learns the dead man was last seen at the wharf after the early bell, which puts him there when the cargo slipped through.

scenes.title: The Board
scenes.summary: Cato matches the early bell, the key logs and the smuggler's testimony and confronts Osric before the Board.
scenes.goal: Prove Osric sold the early curfew and killed the lamplighter who saw it.
scenes.outcome: Osric's alibi fails when the key logs and the smuggler place the dead man at the wharf while Osric held the gate key.

scenes.title: The Honest Bell
scenes.summary: The Board strips Osric of his key; Marguerite and the Guild reopen the lamp-houses, and Cato resets the curfew bell to the tide tables.
scenes.conflict: The Board resists admitting the trade.
scenes.outcome: Osric is dismissed and the curfew bell follows the tide tables again.

evidence_quotes: Osric, the Guild master, hands Cato the Guild's key logs
Master of the Lamplighters' Guild, who holds one of the keys to every lamp-house
labels.rationale: The scene gives Osric the role the cast gives Marguerite.
labels.correction_hint: Have Marguerite hand over the key logs.

evidence_summary: The key-logs scene calls Osric the Guild master although the cast establishes Marguerite as guild master and Osric as a Harbour Board officer.
